verdict.rationale: ReelMimic's own docs say it breaks a reference video down into its camera moves and shows a storyboard plan that you revise in chat before approving. So camera motion is driven by the reference and user feedback rather than left to the model, but no explicit per-shot camera controls are documented. Missing for 10: documented explicit camera-move controls (pan, zoom, orbit, static) per shot, evidence that chat or storyboard edits reliably change camera motion, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a creator, I can direct camera moves (pan, zoom, orbit, static) instead of accepting whatever motion the model picks

citations.quote: Breaks down the reference. Shot count, shot lengths, BPM, transitions, colors, framing and camera moves.
Shows you the plan first. Storyboard, characters, assets and a few style frames. Chat about it until you like it, then approve.
If you want changes, say so in the chat on the right.
